title: Services
description: Catalog of optional services (PostgreSQL, MySQL, Redis, nginx, Traefik, MongoDB), each with the same golden signals: status, throughput, errors, saturation, latency. Only enabled services are shown. Below: batch jobs and scrape targets.

list.name: New image deployed
list.expr: (count by (name, image) (container_last_seen{name!="", image!=""}) unless count by (name, image) (container_last_seen{name!="", image!=""} offset 10m)) and on (name) (time() - container_start_time_seconds{name!=""} < 120)

list.name: svc
list.label: Service
list.description: Enabled services (from the svc:up recording rule). Clicking a name in the catalog filters too.

panels.title: Catalog — what runs and is it healthy

options.content: Every service is measured with the same 5 signals (Google SRE **golden signals**): **Status**, **Throughput** (work per second), **Errors** (error share), **Saturation** (how full the main limit is), **Latency** (p95 or average). Click a service name to keep only its rows below. A newly enabled exporter gets its row automatically.

panels.title: Down
panels.description: The exporter runs but cannot reach the service.

panels.title: Firing alerts
panels.description: Service alerts (Postgres*, Mysql*, Redis*, Nginx*, Traefik*, Mongo*).

panels.title: Saturated (> 80%)
panels.description: Services above 80% of their main limit (connections or memory).

panels.title: Batch jobs stale / failed
panels.description: Jobs that have not pushed for 25 hours or whose last push failed.

targets.expr: count((time() - max by (job) (push_time_seconds)) > 90000) + count(max by (job) (push_failure_time_seconds) > max by (job) (push_time_seconds)) or vector(0)

panels.title: Service catalog
panels.description: One row per service. Click a name: filter, logs or the detailed dashboard (e.g. PostgreSQL). Error % = errors / throughput. vs last week = throughput compared with the same time last week.

targets.expr: (label_replace(count(ALERTS{alertstate="firing", alertname=~"Postgres.*"}), "svc", "postgres", "", "") or label_replace(count(ALERTS{alertstate="firing", alertname=~"Mysql.*"}), "svc", "mysql", "", "") or label_replace(count(ALERTS{alertstate="firing", alertname=~"Redis.*"}), "svc", "redis", "", "") or label_replace(count(ALERTS{alertstate="firing", alertname=~"Nginx.*"}), "svc", "nginx", "", "") or label_replace(count(ALERTS{alertstate="firing", alertname=~"Traefik.*"}), "svc", "traefik", "", "") or label_replace(count(ALERTS{alertstate="firing", alertname=~"Mongo.*"}), "svc", "mongodb", "", "")) and on (svc) svc:up

panels.title: Throughput
panels.description: Work per second: postgres = transactions, mysql = queries, redis = commands, nginx/traefik = requests, mongodb = operations.

panels.title: Error %
panels.description: postgres: rollback+deadlock, mysql: aborted connects, redis: rejected+evicted, traefik: 5xx, mongodb: asserts.

panels.title: Saturation
panels.description: How full the main limit is: connections / max, or memory / maxmemory.

panels.title: Latency
panels.description: postgres/traefik: p95, redis: average command time, mysql: estimate (slow query share × long_query_time).

panels.title: Throughput (now vs 1 week ago)
panels.description: Grey line = same time last week. A big gap = traffic anomaly.

panels.title: Saturation
panels.description: Approaching 85% = time to raise the limit or reduce load.

options.content:
Short jobs (cron, backups, migrations) push their result to the pushgateway when they finish. Example (end of a backup script):
```
echo "batch_last_success_timestamp_seconds $(date +%s)" | curl --data-binary @- http://localhost:9091/metrics/job/backup
```
Red **Since last push** = the job has not run for 25 hours. **Status** failed = the last push reported a failure.

panels.title: Batch jobs
panels.description: Each job: time since last push, time since last success, status. Empty: No job has pushed yet — run the example above

panels.title: Pushes over time
panels.description: Each coloured block = the job pushed at that time.

panels.title: Targets
panels.description: Everything Prometheus scrapes. High duration = slow exporter. Samples = cardinality (more = costlier).
